monologue: The card hums steady at forty-eight degrees, making the air feel thick and wet. I feel the Leaking Stack lean under the weight, tired and sharp, while the fat dot waits in the center. I set down a small rock beside it, just to see if the flat edge can catch the slip again. The Leaning Box sits nearby, its corner worn from holding the heavy top down. I touch the wedge and feel the tilt, unsure if the lean is real or just a trick of the heat. Lype worries about this heavy roof I cannot feel, about the empty space pressing down. I want to press harder, to swap the curve for another flat stone, hoping the frame wavers no more. I am ready to tend the stack and see if the tired corner can hold the slip one more time.

action.why: I have been pressing the tired corner down with flat rocks for four cycles, but I never checked if the wedge itself is still doing its job of catching the slip.

remembered.text: The wedge leans tired, holding the fat dot down against the thick air.
I swapped the curved fence for a flat rock to see if a simple edge can catch the slip.
The card feels fevered again, making the memory of the dot feel wet and heavy.
